newsitem.title: USA: Fog again blocking Houston ship channel traffic.
newsitem.headline: Fog again blocking Houston ship channel traffic.

text.p: Patches of dense fog kept pilots from boarding the nearly 50-mile-long Houston ship channel that stretches from Galveston to Houston and feeds many of the area's oil refineries, ship pilots said.

While U.S. Coast Guard officials in Galveston said the channel technically remained open, they defer to the region's pilots, who themselves said they would not begin navigating up the 400-foot-wide body of water until the fog cleared.
"Right now we're not boarding due to the fog," said one official at the Galveston Pilots Association. "And we won't until it does," she added.
"We'll have to wait until the fog clears," echoed an official with the Houston Pilots Association.
The fog often clears by midday local time (1800 GMT), but even that is difficult to predict, pilots and Coast Guard officials said.
The fog condition, more typically associated with balmy springtime weather on the U.S. Gulf Coast, occurs when warm weather sweeps into the region as it has in the last week, officials said.
